_README: TEMPLATE — copy one item into data/battery-tester/methods.json or data/echem/methods.json and edit. The five blocks instrument / cell / appliedSignal / response / processing / interpretation are the §34 separation made structural: they cannot be accidentally blurred because the renderer reads them separately.

items.name: Full name of the technique
aliases: what your instrument's software calls it
items._comment_instrument: THE INSTRUMENT — what the box controls and measures. Never blur this with what happens in the cell.

instrument.configuration: two-electrode (device level) | three-electrode (material level) | either, stating which

items._comment_cell: THE CELL — what physically happens, and what it depends on.

cell.whatHappens: Plain description of the process at the electrode and in the electrolyte.

items._comment_signal: THE APPLIED SIGNAL — what is imposed, and the parameters that define it.

appliedSignal.waveform: e.g. triangular potential sweep, current step, small-amplitude AC

parameters.name: Parameter name
parameters.guidance: What it controls, what happens if it is too high, what happens if it is too low. Give the reasoning, never a bare recommended number — the student should be able to choose it themselves and check their choice.

items._comment_response: THE RESPONSE — what comes back, and what it is plotted as.
items._comment_processing: DATA PROCESSING — how raw measurements become parameters. Reference formulas by id; never restate an equation here.

steps: What you do to the raw data, in order

items._comment_interpretation: SCIENTIFIC INTERPRETATION — the Learn/Research pair. Two views of one record.

interpretation.learnMode: Plain language. What the result tells you, with no unexplained jargon.
interpretation.researchMode: The mathematical treatment, what the parameters mean physically, and how to judge whether the result is trustworthy.

items._comment_required: The health check warns if limitations is empty. Every technique has limits; writing them down is what stops a student over-reading a result.
limitations: Conditions under which this technique does NOT give a meaningful answer
commonMistakes: The error people actually make, and what it looks like in the data
applications: What this technique is genuinely good for
